records.c: Current level digit source. Incremented at $2BBF and copied into the disk filenames at $C8BF.
Set to $FF by the title interrupt at $1E2F. Multiple main-loop paths clear it and wait for it to become nonzero.
Character-pointer low bits selected by the loading display code at $C889.
Display text for the one-player menu choice. Stored in lowercase byte values and rendered in the game's display font.
Display text for the two-player menu choice.
Display text for the menu's music switch.
Display text for the menu's text pacing switch.
Warm entry after the packed loader. Runs $2001, then sets the initial level number to 0 before the engine's main reset path.
Reinitializes the engine after the level loader. Resets SP, clears the hardware stack and zero page, selects RAM under the system ROMs with I/O visible, and initializes the CIA2 timers.

Saves the registers and switches in I/O. When the band index is zero it refreshes title sprites when enabled and sets the two frame flags. It selects the multicolour pair from the band index and schedules the next raster compare.
Selects the video settings for the bottom panel, saving the previous character pointer. Preloads sprite slots 2 through 7 with shape $B5 and toggles the display around the panel boundary.
Takes a sorted object slot from X loaded at $1D and the current VIC sprite register offset from $D3. Copies position, colour and shape to the selected slot and cycles through offsets $04 through $0E.
Sets the $0458 flag to $FF only when clear, then restores A and returns from interrupt.
Reads CIA1 port A or B indexed by X and inverts the active-low inputs. Sets $0FF4 on fire and resolves the four direction bits to signed axis steps using the selected mapping at $1001 or $1017.
Iterates over nine coordinate pairs beginning at $0210 and $0219 and copies sixteen bytes per entry using the source and destination index orders at $0222 and $0232.
Converts the held-fire state into a fresh press using the previous state. Checks the per-weapon limits, chooses projectile data by ship flags and calls $2DC2 for each eligible shot.
Scans the active projectile slots and active object slots. Uses the separation of the positions and their extents on each axis to decide whether to dispatch a hit.
Hides the sprites, clears per-level flags and invokes $C8B0 to load the assets named by $0442. Restores the SID volume nibble, conditionally queues sound 3 and transfers to $C61A.
The title font tiles, eight bytes per tile. $C4F4 writes four tile numbers for each letter, two from $1531 and two from $1581. The VIC character pointer selects this bank during the loading display.
Character codes 128 through 255 in the title font bank. The upper and lower tile-code pairs may select these tiles without changing the VIC character-bank base.
Consumes outstanding terrain inserts via $9ED8 or uses the current scroll state to choose a new direction or prepare the next wrapped buffer coordinates.
Sets the direction-change flag and 32-step counter, advances the direction index and reads the new direction at $8004,Y. Selects the corresponding buffer setup.
Fetches the next block ID through $9F7A. Multiplies the ID by 25 and adds $EF70. Copies five groups of five character codes into the circular screen staging buffer with width 45 and height 26.
At step 31 advances the $B2/$B3 pointer by 32. Uses the current direction in $AB to choose one of the three index lists at $1023, $1043 and $1063 and returns the block ID from the selected strip.
Starts the scroll counter at 31 and calls $9ED8 for eight groups of four blocks. The destination columns and rows advance by five characters per block.
Takes the text record address in Y:A, decodes its display position and colour setup, and passes characters to the glyph renderer.
Maps the input byte to a glyph index, with separate cases for space, dollar, digits and letters. Writes two successive character codes to each of two rows at ($AE) and applies $0460 as the colour.
Enables all eight title sprites, clears expansion and multicolour mode, and copies positions, pointers and colours to the VIC and the pointer table at $47F8.
Selects the loading screen's scroll, character pointer and colours, then transfers control to $CB40 after setting the text delay state.

Saves $046B, sets up the loading display and writes the level number into four filenames. For the disk path it banks in KERNAL, clears zero-page locations $02 through $FF and calls SETNAM and LOAD for each file, copying the last page of CHARS to $6F00. It restores $046B and the game memory configuration before returning.
Takes the binary level number at $0442 and installs the ASCII digit in the four KERNAL filenames and the loading message.
Seven-byte KERNAL filename for the block file. The final character at $C9BD is replaced by the level digit.
Six-byte KERNAL filename for the character file. The final character at $C9C3 receives the level digit.
Six-byte KERNAL filename for the level file. The final character at $C9C9 receives the level digit.
Five-byte KERNAL filename for the data file. The final character at $C9CE receives the level digit.
Samples the screen characters covered by the hull, checks the solid bit mask at $8024, then calls $CAA6 to test the glyph pixels for contact.

Builds the address of the selected terrain glyph at $5000 plus eight times the character code. Tests its eight pixel rows against the positioned mask and returns $FF when a row changes under the mask.
Fills the two VIC screen pages and $5B00 through $5FFF with $0464. Fills the colour-RAM pages from $0460.

Selects the level parameters using $0442, enables sprite multicolour, and copies the indexed setup tables to working storage. Clears the display, sets up the players and terrain and initializes the object arrays.
Takes two addresses from the first four bytes at $8000 and writes them into the LDA operands at $DCA3 and $DCA8 while RAM under I/O is selected.
Reads ten 16-byte high-score records starting at $1BD3. Displays the three score bytes as pairs of digits and copies the following thirteen name bytes.
Copies 13 bytes from the entry's name into the screen destination, then advances both pointers by 13.
Compares three bytes of a candidate at $1BCF against each 16-byte table entry from $1BD3 and stops where the candidate outranks the existing score.
Two-byte dispatch targets for the command in $05AF,X. $D596 doubles that value and jumps indirectly through the selected entry.
Compares the low six bits of the next event at ($B8) with the scrolling step in $AC, and dispatches on its high two bits. $3E terminates and $3F advances the stream at the step rollover.
Finds a spare slot, reads the position and colour from the eight-byte scroll event, installs the movement and parameter pointers, then advances the event cursor by eight.
Reads the first two bytes of an object parameter record via ($AE) and decodes the second byte into a three-bit class and separate flag fields for slot X.
Claims a slot, copies the two coordinate bytes and extracts the event flags. Selects an indexed set of level parameters and advances the scroll-event cursor by four.
Passes zero position offsets to the slot constructor and advances the scroll-event cursor by seven.
For slot X, rotates the X component through carry and adds the slot's X offset. Shifts the Y component right and adds the slot's Y offset. Writes the results to $05BF,X and $05CF,X.
Copies the slot's stream pointer from $067F and $068F to $AE/$AF. Doubles the command selector at $05AF,X and jumps through the little-endian dispatch table at $D000.
Adds the byte count in A to the slot's 16-bit script address, mirrors it to $AE/$AF and reads the next command.
Clears the active slot and its Y coordinate, decrements the active-object count and releases the cached sprite frames reserved by the object.
Takes the delay from the byte after the opcode when the slot's timer is zero. Decrements the timer and advances the script by two when it expires.
Reads signed X and Y increments and advances by three bytes when the immediate-motion mode is set. The other path initializes a timed movement.
Changes the slot's X and Y by the signed deltas in $02 and $03. An unsigned carry or borrow on the X byte flips the high X flag.
Reads a little-endian address from the next two bytes, updates the slot's script pointer and immediately dispatches the new opcode.
Loads the next byte into the slot's repeat register at $06DF,X and dispatches the opcode two bytes later.
Decrements the slot repeat register. If nonzero, subtracts the operand from the script pointer and dispatches there. Otherwise it advances two bytes.
Sets the slot's immediate-motion flag at $06EF,X and continues at the next opcode.
Clears the slot's immediate-motion flag and advances the stream by one.
Initializes the per-slot motion parameters from seven operand bytes when the timer is zero. Snapshots the starting position, runs the position calculation, and leaves the original position restored.
Calls the screen operation at $3A81, sets $0499, then moves the stream pointer ahead one byte and clears the slot timer.
Releases the previous cached frames. Installs the command's one-byte frame number and sets the index and timer to make the animation pass reload that frame.
Reads the sound index from the command operand. Calls $1E00 when the mode flag permits sound effects, then advances the object stream by two.
Advances active slot animation timers, steps or reverses frame indices according to the animation flags, and requests an expanded sprite when the frame is not already cached.
Claims a sprite cache slot. Looks up the level frame's two-byte address via the patched table loads, clears its leading blank bytes, copies the packed record, and fills the remainder with zero.
Chooses the $4000 or $4400 screen matrix from the active page bit. Rewrites the unrolled source addresses for the circular row offset before copying rows from the staging buffer into the screen.
A zero request disables the sound update and one transfers to the tick entry. The other requests call the selector at $ECB0, clear the voice and SID working state, then enable the update.
Tests the enable operand, advances the tempo and pattern counters, and walks three voice slots. It reads a different pattern sequence for each voice and resolves pattern pointers through $FB56.

Shared SID pattern bytes. $E271 and $E2FC read through addresses installed from $FB56. In the first stream $9F has bit 7 set and acts as a wait byte, while a note selects an instrument byte on the next read.
Later SID patterns in the same bytecode store. The pointer entries near $FBD0 select patterns in this region, and the voice parser at $E29B uses the bytes as notes and control tokens.
Shared little-endian SID pattern addresses. $E253 and $E25C patch the voice stream loaders at $E271 and $E2FC with the selected pair.
